titleEn: PerPlant lands Valtra deal to put its AI crop sensor on tractors straight from the factory
titleZh: PerPlant与Valtra达成合作，AI作物传感器实现拖拉机出厂预装
summaryZh: 丹麦农业科技初创公司PerPlant与AGCO旗下Valtra Unlimited达成合作，其AI作物传感器将出厂预装于Valtra多款拖拉机。该传感器通过双摄像头扫描作物，生成地图并支持实时精准喷洒、变量施肥等作业，可减少40%-87%的投入品使用。PerPlant同时正在构建Nexus数据平台，旨在汇聚田间厘米级数据，为农艺师和投入品公司提供AI工具开发基础。此举标志着精准农业硬件与主机厂深度整合的趋势。
featuredReason: 该新闻展示了AI作物传感器与主流拖拉机品牌出厂预装的深度整合案例，以及从硬件销售向田间数据平台转型的商业模式，对智慧畜牧及种植业从业者理解精准农业技术落地路径和主机厂合作模式具有参考价值。
contentFull:
Danish agtech startup PerPlant’s AI crop sensor is now available factory-fitted onto new Valtra tractors through a partnership with Valtra Unlimited, the customization studio of the AGCO-owned tractor brand.

The sensor will be offered on Valtra’s A105 and A115, G, N, T, Q and S Series models in selected European markets, and in other markets on request. Sales begin this month alongside the launch of Valtra’s new sixth-generation T Series.

With farming margins always on the thin side, many prefer to buy a crop intelligence system that fits onto equipment they already have, says PerPlant CEO and cofounder Rasmus Emil Hansen.

“They’re not going to go out and buy the newest sprayer just to have it, because it’s quite a big investment for them.”

The deal also puts PerPlant’s cameras on more tractors at a time when the company is betting its long-term value lies less in spraying and more in the field data its sensors collect every time a tractor drives.

“That is a huge milestone for us,” Hansen tells AgFunderNews. “We have worked on these relations for some years.”

The relationship started in Finland’s BioBoosters accelerator, where Valtra selected a small group of European startups to work with. PerPlant has made repeated trips to Finland since.

‘Eyes’ on the tractor

PerPlant’s sensor is a single AI unit with two cameras that mount onto the tractor roof. As the tractor drives, the sensor scans the crop and turns that data into maps and possible real-time actions to take. These include spot spraying of weeds and variable-rate application of fertilizer, fungicide and growth regulator, day or night. The sensor also tracks biomass, weeds and risk zones over the season and uploads that data to farm management systems.

It works with ISOBUS sprayers, spreaders and seeders. It can also be used alongside other tools in Valtra’s precision farming ecosystem, including those from PTx, AGCO’s precision ag brand.

PerPlant says farmers using its system have cut input use by 40% to 87%, depending on the implement. Average operating cost is around €4 ($4.4) per hectare on a 200-hectare farm.

“Most farmers want precision farming, but not the cost and complexity that usually comes with it,” Hansen said in a statement.

Tomi Siljander, manager of product engineering at Valtra Unlimited, said in a statement that customers “increasingly expect smart solutions that help them farm more precisely and more profitably.”

Building a ‘world model’ of the field

Hansen and Sumod Nandanwar founded PerPlant in Copenhagen in 2022. The company now has dealers in more than 10 countries across Europe as well as in Chile and Argentina. Its sensors have mapped more than 250,000 hectares across 12 countries.

PerPlant also recently announced a strategic partnership with US-based precision ag company Ag Leader, which showcased PerPlant’s sensor at the recent Farm Progress Show in Iowa. The two companies are building an integration aimed at improving spot spraying and variable-rate application.

PerPlant started out selling see-and-spray as a low-cost retrofit. Along the way, Hansen says, the company realized its sensors were also collecting something valuable: season-long, centimeter-level field data.

“It’s costly to just map, because someone has to be out on that field, and the system which is mostly out there is the tractor,” he says.

To make use of that data, PerPlant is building Nexus, which will let agronomists, input companies and others who serve farmers access PerPlant’s field data and build their own tailored AI tools. PerPlant has validated the product with the largest agricultural cooperative in the Netherlands, and Nexus is slated to go into production early next year.

“Fundamentally, over time we hope to build a world model of the fields, similar to how you use Google Earth,” Hansen says.

PerPlant recently raised a €1 million ($1.2 million) round and is now raising €5 million ($5.8 million). The company is also considering entering the US as soon as next season, though Hansen says its focus for now is executing through its European channels.

translationZh:
丹麦农业科技初创公司PerPlant的AI作物传感器现已通过与被AGCO拥有的拖拉机品牌Valtra的定制工作室Valtra Unlimited的合作，实现出厂预装于全新Valtra拖拉机。

该传感器将在部分欧洲市场的Valtra A105和A115、G、N、T、Q及S系列车型上提供，其他市场可按需订购。销售于本月启动，恰逢Valtra新一代第六代T系列发布。

PerPlant首席执行官兼联合创始人Rasmus Emil Hansen表示，由于农业利润始终偏薄，许多人更倾向于购买能适配现有设备的作物智能系统。

“他们不会仅仅为了拥有最新款喷雾机而去购买它，因为这对他们来说是一笔相当大的投资。”

这笔交易还使PerPlant的摄像头装上了更多拖拉机，而该公司正押注其长期价值较少在于喷洒，更多在于传感器每次拖拉机行驶时收集的田间数据。

“这对我们来说是一个巨大的里程碑，”Hansen告诉AgFunderNews。“我们为这些关系已经努力了几年。”

这段关系始于芬兰的BioBoosters加速器，Valtra在那里挑选了一小群欧洲初创公司进行合作。此后PerPlant多次前往芬兰。

**拖拉机上的‘眼睛’**

PerPlant的传感器是一个单一的AI单元，配有两个摄像头，安装在拖拉机顶部。当拖拉机行驶时，传感器扫描作物并将数据转化为地图和可能的实时行动建议。这些包括白天或夜间对杂草的定点喷洒，以及肥料、杀菌剂和生长调节剂的变量施用。传感器还跟踪整个季节的生物量、杂草和风险区域，并将数据上传至农场管理系统。

它可与ISOBUS喷雾机、撒肥机和播种机配合使用。它还可以与Valtra精准农业生态系统中的其他工具一起使用，包括来自AGCO精准农业品牌PTx的工具。

PerPlant称，使用其系统的农民根据机具不同，已将投入品使用量减少了40%至87%。在200公顷的农场上，平均运营成本约为每公顷4欧元（4.4美元）。

“大多数农民想要精准农业，但不想要通常随之而来的成本和复杂性，”Hansen在一份声明中说。

Valtra Unlimited产品工程经理Tomi Siljander在一份声明中表示，客户“越来越期待智能解决方案，帮助他们更精准、更盈利地耕作。”

**构建田间的‘世界模型’**

Hansen和Sumod Nandanwar于2022年在哥本哈根创立了PerPlant。该公司现已在欧洲10多个国家以及智利和阿根廷拥有经销商。其传感器已在12个国家测绘了超过25万公顷的土地。

PerPlant最近还宣布与总部位于美国的精准农业公司Ag Leader建立战略合作伙伴关系，后者在最近的艾奥瓦州Farm Progress展会上展示了PerPlant的传感器。两家公司正在构建一项集成，旨在改善定点喷洒和变量施用。

PerPlant最初以低成本改装方式销售见草喷洒系统。Hansen说，在此过程中，公司意识到其传感器还在收集一些有价值的东西：贯穿整个季节的厘米级田间数据。

“仅仅测绘成本很高，因为必须有人在那块田里，而通常在那里的系统主要是拖拉机，”他说。

为了利用这些数据，PerPlant正在构建Nexus，它将让农艺师、投入品公司和其他为农民服务的人能够访问PerPlant的田间数据并构建自己的定制AI工具。PerPlant已在荷兰最大的农业合作社验证了该产品，Nexus计划于明年初投入生产。

“从根本上说，随着时间的推移，我们希望构建一个田间的世界模型，类似于你使用谷歌地球的方式，”Hansen说。

PerPlant最近筹集了100万欧元（120万美元）的一轮融资，目前正在筹集500万欧元（580万美元）。该公司还在考虑最早于下一季进入美国市场，不过Hansen表示目前重点是执行其欧洲渠道。
author: Jennifer Marston
